body: Standard Lebanese licence plates can be long or short and have a blue strip on the left, similar to European plates. Taxi licence plates are a distinct deep red.
The official language of Lebanon is Arabic, but English and French are also commonly seen.
Lebanon is the only Middle Eastern country with official low-quality 'shitcam' coverage.
Aside from the 'shitcam' coverage, all other footage in Lebanon was captured with a Generation 3 trekker.
Lebanon has a Mediterranean landscape with many hills and rocky cliffs.
Lebanon uses various utility poles, including metallic mesh poles which are sometimes painted bright yellow, and standard wooden poles.
Many buildings in Lebanon are constructed with sandstone bricks, which can resemble the Jerusalem stone found in Israel and the West Bank.
Most of the Street View coverage is concentrated near the west coast, in the area north of Beirut.
The region around Zahle is characterized by flat agricultural fields, with mountains visible to the northwest.
Coverage showing snow is found in the northeastern mountains, east of Tripoli.
Northern Lebanon is very flat and agricultural, with mountains sometimes visible to the southeast.
A visible black car can be seen in the coverage in and around Zahle.
The Generation 3 trekker coverage in Lebanon is extremely limited, mainly focusing on tourist attractions, university campuses, and trails.
Beirut is the capital and the only covered city with many modern high-rise buildings. Urban infrastructure is almost always visible in the background.
Coverage along the Beirut promenade features a grey brick pavement and a large number of fan palms.
Université Saint Joseph, southeast of central Beirut, is recognizable by its old, grand-looking sandstone building.
The Debbieh campus of the Beirut Arab University has large, modern sandstone buildings on a forested hill. The ocean can often be seen in the distance to the west.
The Lebanese International University (LIU) is identified by its large stone buildings with unpainted bottom floors and beige-painted upper floors.
The University of Balamand has many modern, white-painted buildings that often have a cubic appearance.
The Lebanese American University, east of Byblos, has a very urban feel with extensive construction and large, modern buildings.
The ancient city of Byblos, one of the world's oldest, is recognized by its many historical buildings constructed from a uniform type of unpainted stone bricks.
The trekker coverage near Bsharri is identifiable by the large canyon to the south.
In Baalbek, you can find a large complex of Roman ruins.
The Mseilha fortress, southwest of Tripoli, is built on a single, massive limestone rock.
The only rural coastal road with trekker coverage in Lebanon is located southwest of Tripoli.
